entries.definition: A contiguous sequence of objects that all have the same element type.
entries.example: In int samples[6], the elements are samples[0] through samples[5].
entries.misconception: The conceptual row of elements is a display of numeric process addresses.

entries.definition: One object in an array, identified by its position; it holds a value of the array's element type.
entries.example: samples[3] is the fourth int object in samples.
entries.misconception: An element and its current integer value are the same thing.

citations.claim: An array is a contiguous set of objects with a member object type called the element type.

entries.definition: An integer subscript that selects an element by its offset from the first element.
entries.example: samples[3] selects the fourth element, when the array has at least four elements.
entries.misconception: An index counts bytes or starts at one.

citations.claim: Subscript evaluation is defined through pointer addition and indirection.

entries.definition: The permitted range of elements in an array or pointer-plus-count view.
entries.example: For six readings, the readable indices are 0 through 5; the project API also caps count at 30.
entries.misconception: Extra physical capacity means a function may ignore the count supplied by its caller.

citations.claim: C pointer arithmetic in this context is restricted to the array range and the one-past position.

entries.definition: A value that can refer to an object; pointers to array elements can also identify positions within that array.
entries.example: For a four-element int array, samples + 2 points to element index 2.
entries.misconception: A pointer's numeric representation is the teaching model for an array index.

citations.claim: Pointer addition within an array is specified in units of the pointed-to type and is bounded by the array.

entries.definition: A pointer to the position immediately after the last element of an array; it can mark the end but cannot be read as an element.
entries.example: For int samples[6], samples + 6 may be formed and compared within the allowed rules, but not dereferenced.
entries.misconception: The one-past position is a seventh element with an unpredictable value.

citations.claim: One-past pointer formation is permitted, but evaluation as an element is not.

entries.definition: An explicit number of elements that a caller makes available to a pointer-based function.
entries.example: sum_values(samples, 6) receives a pointer and the number of readable elements.
entries.misconception: A function can recover the original array length from its pointer parameter.

citations.claim: An array parameter is adjusted to a pointer parameter; the count is a separate API value.

entries.definition: The C rule that adjusts an array parameter declaration to a pointer parameter to the element type.
entries.example: In int total(const int values[], size_t count), values is adjusted to a pointer parameter.
entries.misconception: The brackets in a function parameter preserve the caller's array length.

citations.claim: The function parameter's array type is adjusted to a pointer type.
